title: Aggregates computed in the service
description: The repository offers only get/list/create/update/upsert/delete and the source allows one table. Stats, currencies, effective date and history statistics are computed in the service from list operations.

options.label: Single rates table, list operations, aggregate in service

title: Route precedence for /rates/latest
description: /rates/latest is registered before /rates/{date} so it is not rejected as a malformed date.
system_choice: Register the latest route first in the shared rates router.

title: Invocation with no command
description: The source does not state the status for running fxrates with no arguments; the harness check U1 expects 2.
system_choice: No command is a usage error: exit 2, one stderr line, empty stdout.

title: EUR to EUR with no publication
description: EUR needs no stored rate, but the effective date must still exist.
system_choice: Return 404 when no publication is on or before the date, even when both currencies are EUR.

title: Exit status on SIGTERM
description: The source requires a clean stop on SIGTERM without naming the exit status.
system_choice: Exit 0 after uvicorn shuts down gracefully.

title: Four-slash sqlite URL form is undefined
description: DATABASE_URL=sqlite:////abs/path strips to //abs/path, which Path keeps as a double-slash path. The spec defines only a file path with an optional sqlite:// prefix, so I tested the sqlite:///abs form. Should the four-slash form be normalized to an absolute path?

title: sqlite:// alone is treated as an empty DATABASE_URL
description: After stripping the sqlite:// prefix, an empty remainder is skipped and resolution falls through to DATABASE_PATH. The spec does not state this case. Is that acceptable?

title: fxrates launcher working directory
description: The launcher runs python -m cli in the caller's working directory instead of changing to the application root, so the relative data/app.db default resolves where the user runs it. It only adds the root to PYTHONPATH. Is that acceptable, or should it cd to the root?

title: Indexes derived from the persistence declaration
description: The rendered schema indexes rates(date); rates(currency, date). Each is implied by the declaration — a foreign key is looked up by its child column, and a read pattern's Input fields are the predicate it filters on. Declare an `- INDEX (...)` bullet in DATABASE.md for any index this does not cover.

title: Acceptance criterion live-load-visible-in-rates proves nothing
description:
FEATURE-LiveVisibility.md [live-load-visible-in-rates]: accepts [200, 404]: 404 means the endpoint is absent, so this passes against an application that implements nothing. Assert 404 alone for a negative probe, or assert the status the implementation answers with. (assert before.status_code in (200, 404))

A criterion states one expectation. Pin the status the implementation answers with — a stub that answers is a real contract and a real test — or assert the not-found status alone as a deliberate negative probe. A criterion that needs a row to exist creates it through the public interface first rather than admitting the status that says it never existed.
